messages:
Alex (AE): ACME POC stuck — clients get 413 on /v1/generate when they POST a single request containing ~120 docs. They pasted their curl error, looks like a proxy drop. Need quick unblock for demo tomorrow.

ACME-POC: curl: (22) 413 Request Entity Too Large. Body: {"error":"request entity too large"}. Content-Length: 3,892,148. They go: client -> corp-nginx -> our edge LB -> api.redwood.ai. No compression.

Priya (SE): Thanks. Two immediate suspects: (1) their corp-nginx or our edge LB has a max_body_size limit, (2) some intermediate CDN rejects chunked bodies. Can they try setting Content-Encoding: gzip first? We accept gzipped request bodies.

Tim (Ops): If they need a hotfix, we can raise max_body_size for their dedicated trial instance for a short window. Tell me instance id and target size. Note: changing proxy settings temporarily is fine but not a recommended production pattern.

Jordan (SalesEng): They're trying to avoid building an index and want a single-shot extraction across all docs. That will be costly and fragile. We should suggest a cheap POC design that keeps dev effort low: either gzip + chunking OR do a one-time embed & local search for the demo.

ACME-POC: Instance id ded-ff12. Can you open to 12MB for 8 hours? Also any quick client tips if we can't change infra?

Priya (SE): Client tips: 
1) Gzip the payload. Example: 
```
# POSIX example
printf '%s' "$BIG_JSON" | gzip -c > req.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip"
  --data-binary @req.gz
```
2) Use multipart/form-data to upload several small parts then assemble at app layer (if their gateway handles multipart better).
3) Split into N requests: chunk docs into batches of ~100-200KB per request and either (a) call the model for each chunk to extract facts, then merge, or (b) create embeddings for each doc once and retrieve top-k passages per question.

Tim (Ops): Please confirm ded-ff12 and desired max. I'll file an edge request. Keep in mind some internal NGiNXs reject chunked transfer-encoding; using Content-Length + gzip is the safest.

deploy-bot: Change request CRE-7892 opened by Tim (Ops) to bump max_body_size to 12M on ded-ff12 for 8h (pending edge approval).

ACME-POC: Thanks. If we gzip, roughly how much will size shrink?

Priya (SE): Depends on content; text-heavy docs often compress 6-10x. So 3.9MB could become ~500KB. Quick test: gzip -9 usually gives best compression but is CPU heavier. For the demo, -6 is a good balance.

Jordan (SalesEng): On cost for the POC: embeddings require a one-time embedding pass (cost per token), then small generation calls. One-shot giant prompts balloon token-generation costs. I'll throw together a back-of-envelope comparison and DM ACME.

ACME-POC: While waiting, they tried gzip + content-encoding and got a 200 but the model output was truncated — looks like prompt got cut off. Are we truncating long inputs?

Priya (SE): Two separate limits: (1) transport/proxy size (we just fixed/are fixing) and (2) model context window. The model only ever sees up to its context window; if the combined input tokens exceed the model's context length, the model will truncate the earliest tokens. max_tokens param only limits the output. Recommend picking a model with sufficient window (e.g., 32k) or switching to retrieval for longer corpora.

Tim (Ops): Edge approved CRE-7892 and applied change to ded-ff12. Increased max_body_size to 12M for 8 hours. deploy-bot: CRE-7892 applied.

deploy-bot: CRE-7892 applied to ded-ff12 4:12UTC 4-Mar-2026.

ACME-POC: Re-tested with gzip + smaller batch pattern (split into 6 batches) -> all requests succeeded. Demo green. Thanks!

Priya (SE): Great. Short-term notes for ACME: 
- For demo, gzip + short bump is fine. 
- Long-term: ingest via embeddings + search or build a small pre-processing pipeline to chunk + summarize. That gives predictable cost and avoids dependency on proxy limits. 

Jordan (SalesEng): Action items: 
- I will send the cost comparison and a minimal sample repo for chunking vs embeddings. 
- Priya to share gzip + multipart examples to the ACME POC thread. 
- Tim to schedule rollback of the proxy bump in 8 hours and document change.

Alex (AE): Perfect. I'll notify ACME and mark this POC blocker resolved. :thumbsup:
